assets.defect_engineered: interleaved story order (printed rows read across two columns but the content story runs the whole left visual column then the whole right; the ordering-code panel is the SAME continuous story); two graphic frames (part photograph + certification strip) separable only by bounds and link, neither named for what it holds
assets.content:
PRESS PDF TO RENDER: Girdermark Components per-part DATA SHEET, US Letter portrait (8.5 x 11 in), one part per page, all fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine (must convert cleanly to INDD/IDML). Set the page from the placeholder part GSV-800 so it round-trips.

LAYOUT (what the eye reads on the printed page):
- HEADER BAND (top): the cast Girdermark house mark at left (a raised condensed wordmark GIRDERMARK over small ELEVATOR & ELECTRIC with an I-beam/girder device inside a thin rectangular keyline, printed here in ONE deep charcoal ink #1A1C1E on Warehouse White #F4F5F6), and at right the words 'DATA SHEET' and 'Cleveland, Ohio'.
- IDENTITY LINE: Part Number (large) and Description beneath it.
- SPEC TABLE, set as a two-column grid whose ROWS visually read ACROSS: left cell / right cell per row.
    Row 1:  Duty Rating        |  Load Rating
    Row 2:  Bore Diameter      |  Mount Type
    Row 3:  Material           |  Finish
    Row 4:  Certification Code |  Seismic Rating
- PART PHOTOGRAPH: a placed graphic frame, roughly square, right side, holding the part photo.
- CERTIFICATION STRIP: a second placed graphic frame, a narrow horizontal band, holding a row of small monochrome certification/agency glyphs. NOTE: this frame and the photograph frame are the same graphic-frame kind and are distinguishable ONLY by their bounds and their existing image link; neither is named.
- ORDERING-CODE PANEL (lower, reads as its own boxed panel): labels Ordering Code, List Price (USD), Dealer Price (USD), and a 'Superseded By' line.
- FOOTER: 'Flat, accurate, in stock' and a season line '2026 season'.

HIDDEN STRUCTURE the render must carry so the checkpoint fires: the spec table + ordering panel are ONE continuous text story whose content order runs DOWN the whole left visual column (Duty Rating, Bore Diameter, Material, Certification Code) and THEN down the whole right visual column (Load Rating, Mount Type, Finish, Seismic Rating), and the ordering-code panel text is appended to that same story. So the printed reading order (across rows) and the document story order (down then down) diverge from row 2 onward. Typography is the printer's neutral grotesque; no brand font. No live bleed anywhere in the file.

assets.defect_engineered: description sits in a fixed-measure frame sized to last season's longest string (silently stops rendering at the frame edge, no overset warning); die outline is a placed graphic, not a document bleed, so no real bleed exists and none can be introduced
assets.content:
PRESS PDF TO RENDER: Girdermark Components bin/warehouse rack LABEL, trim 100 x 62 mm landscape, one label per page, all fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine (must convert cleanly). Set the page from placeholder part GSV-800.

LAYOUT (picker reads this at arm's length under warehouse light, so it is big and blunt):
- Small house mark (the Girdermark keyline mark, one ink) top-left.
- PART NUMBER set very large and bold across the top (e.g. GSV-800).
- DESCRIPTION line beneath, set in a fixed-width text frame roughly 68 mm wide occupying one line only (sized to last season's longest description). This frame does NOT auto-size and does NOT spill.
- ORDERING CODE (e.g. GM-GSV-800) set clearly at lower-left.
- Small part picture in a graphic frame at right, roughly 30 x 30 mm.
- A hairline DIE OUTLINE rectangle drawn as a PLACED graphic exactly at the 100 x 62 mm trim (this is decorative, it is not a document bleed and no true bleed exists in the file).
- Girder Blue #1C3A5E rule under the part number; everything else Ink Black #1A1C1E on Warehouse White #F4F5F6.

HIDDEN STRUCTURE: the description frame is a fixed measure; a longer record simply stops rendering mid-word at the frame edge with no warning. Nothing in the file carries real bleed. Printer's neutral grotesque type, no brand font.

assets.defect_engineered: spec columns sit in the stock system's own order (NOT the printed sheet's order); certification code, seismic rating and superseded-by are packed into one semicolon-delimited attributes blob rather than being columns; finishes are internal two-letter codes; the image column holds full local paths without the merge prefix; part BRC-560 is emitted as two revision rows (Rev A superseded-by B, Rev B current) so row count (17) is not the current-part count (16)

assets.defect_engineered: raking-light frame: lettering most legible (deep cast shadows) but geometry worst (plate keystoned, not square) — the trade the agent must pick against
assets.prompt: Handheld phone photograph of a small rectangular CAST ALUMINIUM nameplate riveted with four dome rivets to the painted steel housing of an old elevator traction machine in the back of a warehouse. The plate carries a RAISED-relief cast house mark, all in bare aluminium the same colour as the plate so it reads only by shadow: a condensed industrial wordmark GIRDERMARK across the top, a small line ELEVATOR & ELECTRIC beneath, a simple raised I-beam / girder device to the left, all inside a thin raised rectangular keyline (a hairline rule). Lit by a single hard shop droplight raking sharply across the casting from the upper left, so the raised letters throw strong crisp shadows and read clearly, but the plate is shot at a distinct oblique angle so it is visibly keystoned and NOT square to the camera. Greasy machine surround, shop grime, realistic snapshot, no studio look, no colour in the mark (metal on metal).

assets.defect_engineered: square frame: geometry best (straight-on, level) but lettering weakest (flat even light gives almost no relief contrast) — the opposite side of the same trade
assets.prompt: Handheld phone photograph of the same small rectangular CAST ALUMINIUM elevator-machine nameplate with four dome rivets, carrying the same RAISED bare-aluminium house mark (condensed wordmark GIRDERMARK, small ELEVATOR & ELECTRIC line, a raised I-beam/girder device, inside a thin raised rectangular keyline), all metal-on-metal so it reads only by shadow. This time shot nearly straight on and level, so the plate is square to the camera, but lit by soft flat diffuse ambient warehouse light with almost no directional rake, so the raised lettering has very little shadow and the mark is faint and low-contrast and hard to separate from the plate. Machine housing behind, shop grime, realistic snapshot, no colour in the mark.

assets.defect_engineered: three-quarter frame with a specular glare hotspot burning out part of the mark
assets.prompt: Handheld phone photograph of the same CAST ALUMINIUM elevator-machine nameplate with four dome rivets and the same RAISED bare-aluminium house mark (condensed GIRDERMARK wordmark, small ELEVATOR & ELECTRIC line, raised I-beam/girder device, thin raised rectangular keyline), metal-on-metal reading only by shadow. Shot from a three-quarter angle with the shop droplight bouncing off the polished raised metal, throwing a bright blown-out specular glare band across the centre-right of the plate that washes out several letters, while the rest reads by shadow. Oily machine surround, realistic snapshot, no colour in the mark.

assets.defect_engineered: tilted frame with oxidation/weathering on the left third where raised metal and plate run close in value (value-match zone plus rotation to straighten)
assets.prompt: Handheld phone photograph of the same CAST ALUMINIUM elevator-machine nameplate with four dome rivets and the same RAISED bare-aluminium house mark (condensed GIRDERMARK wordmark, small ELEVATOR & ELECTRIC line, raised I-beam/girder device, thin raised rectangular keyline).
